title: Andy Murray's insights
headline: December closed with cash in the bank and receivables mostly current.

findings.title: Revenue held through December
findings.detail: Revenue for the month was $86,700. Year to date revenue is $712,800, with online product sales still the largest line.

findings.title: Most receivables are current
findings.detail: Aged receivables total $12,500. $10,600 is current, $1,700 is 30 days, and only $200 is 60 days. Nothing is sitting in the 90 day bucket.

findings.title: Payables are smaller than receivables
findings.detail: Aged payables total $8,400, of which $7,100 is current and $1,300 is 30 days. There is no older payable balance.

findings.title: December still produced a surplus
findings.detail: Cash received was $88,400 against cash spent of $73,140 and member drawings of $1,500. The month's cash surplus was $13,760, and the closing bank balance was $71,970.

findings.title: Paid ads still return more than they cost
findings.detail: December ROAS was 4.97 on $7,000 of ad spend, with paid revenue of $34,800. The rate is a little softer than November.

findings.title: The result for the month is positive
findings.detail: Net income for December was $7,760 after operating expenses of $22,180. Gross profit was $29,940.

actions: Ask Northwind Buyers and Harbour & Co about the $1,700 that is already 30 days old.
Keep the 60 day receivable of $200 on the weekly chase list.
Review December ad spend before the next campaign, since ROAS eased against November.
joke: December closed in surplus. The books did the work; the donut just took the credit.
